small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_N tiles (256, 512) and try BLOCK_M=64/128 with BLOCK_K=64 in `gemm_logsumexp_kernel` since N=1024 is small — fewer N tiles means less redundant K-loop work. Also add num_stages=4 variants for the K loop.
- For `gemm_sigmoid_kernel` (M=16384, N=4096, K=2048), add configs with BLOCK_K=64 and BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256 num_warps=8 num_stages=4, plus a GROUP_M=8 block swizzle for better L2 reuse across the N tiles of each row group.
- Pre-transpose W (store as [K, N] contiguous) once in `__init__` so the inner `tl.dot` loads B without `tl.trans`, enabling better vectorized loads in the hot K loop.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the entire pipeline into a single persistent kernel: one program per row-tile of M loops over hidden (N1=4096) computing sigmoid(X@W1+b1) tile-by-tile into registers/shared, then immediately consumes that tile as the "X" of the second GEMM accumulating into a [BLOCK_M, output_size=1024] tile, finishing with online LSE — avoids materializing the [16384, 4096] hidden activation (256MB write+read, the dominant memory traffic).
- Alternatively, since output_size=1024 fits one N-tile, make the second kernel persistent per row-block keeping the [BLOCK_M, 1024] accumulator resident; then the K-reduction over hidden=4096 is the only loop and LSE is a final register reduce — eliminates the n_tiles outer loop and its repeated X loads.
- Consider splitK on the hidden=4096 axis with atomic-free two-stage reduction for kernel 2 if persistent fusion is too complex; the K=4096, N=1024 GEMM is the bottleneck and benefits from more parallelism than just M/BLOCK_M=256 programs.
